description: Live /v1/chat answer for a Japan multi-stop trip, captured as the second itinerary quality target. Unlike the Vietnam target (seeded curated data), every save here came from real TikTok extractions, so the provenance attribution ('from a tiktok') is organic. What must hold: saves pinned per stop, tiktok provenance said out loud, a saved place inside a leg corridor called out as on-the-way (Mount Fuji on Osaka-Tokyo), honest gap for a city with no saves, one closing question.

request.message: im planning a trip to japan, visiting kyoto, then osaka, then tokyo. what should i stop at along the way?

response.message:
nice, you've got some solid saves across the trip. here's how i'd shape it stop by stop.

[Kyoto](kebi://area/jp/kyoto)

you didn't save anything in kyoto yet, so i'd start with the temples and gardens that anchor the city. [Meiji Jingu](kebi://venue/d4104468-7ac7-4674-8b91-a9b1b559fcfb) is actually on your tokyo list, but kyoto's temple scene is where the real depth is, fushimi inari with its thousands of red gates, arashiyama bamboo grove, and the golden pavilion at kinkaku-ji are the classics. since you're there first, hit them in the morning before the crowds build, especially the bamboo grove.

Osaka

you saved [Universal Studios Japan](kebi://venue/e68f1787-c5f6-4ed6-81b1-e0296a02ecf9) from a tiktok, and that's the anchor here. the super mario themed attractions are the draw if you're into that, though it's a full day commitment at the expensive end. if theme parks aren't your thing, osaka's street food scene in dotonbori is the move, takoyaki, okonomiyaki, all of it in one neighborhood.

the leg between Osaka and Tokyo

this is where your trip gets interesting. you've got [Mount Fuji](kebi://venue/67543868-5745-45bd-a5e9-4ab948480e30) saved, and that's genuinely on your way, it's the classic stop, though climbing it is a whole thing. you also saved [The Making of Harry Potter](kebi://venue/3d3d35f0-b134-4c2b-9dc0-e34ecef0576e), which is the Warner Bros. Studio Tour, a two-hour tour for forty-five dollars. [Shinjuku Gyoen](kebi://venue/1cf8682b-9ba4-4cc1-8a07-651c8b8b7b37) is marked as on this leg too, though it's technically in tokyo proper, it's a massive garden with japanese, english, and french landscaping, quiet and worth an afternoon if you need a break from the intensity.

Tokyo

you've got three saves here and they're all tiktok picks: [Shibuya Sky](kebi://venue/1bd47f5c-8855-4ba9-98e6-d4c6ccf6427f) for the city view, [teamLab Planets](kebi://venue/3546d397-b212-4cb4-866a-3a87cd06c485) and [teamLab Borderless](kebi://venue/ce8d6832-b63e-4b15-8d39-50133dabbe62) for the immersive digital art. Shibuya Sky is the quickest (sixteen dollars for the view), while the teamLab experiences are pricier and take longer but are genuinely the kind of thing that stops you, interactive digital art, very instagrammable. Meiji Jingu is also here, the shinto shrine in a forest, peaceful contrast to the neon.

the missing detail: how many nights do you have in each city? that changes whether you're doing kyoto as a quick temple run or staying long enough to explore the geisha districts and smaller gardens.
